title: "Usage — 1D"

The [workflow](usage.qmd) applied to a homogeneous layer stack, in both modes —
free-running and air-conditioned. The examples show **real results** for the average
day of May in Cuernavaca, Mexico (the EPW and `materials.ini` used here live in
`docs/data/` in the repository), and are executed when this documentation is
rendered.

Setup shared by all the examples:

{{< include _usage-setup.qmd >}}

## 1D wall, free-running

```{python}
wall = eh.System(eh.Location(epw_file))
wall.azimuth = 90                    # east-facing
wall.absortance = 0.3
wall.layers = [("Mortero", 0.025), ("Ladrillo", 0.10)]
wall.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
wall.Tsa()

data = wall.solve()                  # free-running Ti
data = pd.concat([data, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)

print(f"energy_transfer = {wall.energy_transfer:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.energy_transfer/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
```

```{python}
plot_day(data, title="Mortero + Ladrillo wall, east, free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

The indoor temperature `Ti` oscillates with a smaller amplitude than the sun–air
temperature `Tsa` and lags behind it — the damping and the delay are the thermal
mass at work.

## 1D wall, air-conditioned

Same wall; `solveAC()` holds `Ti` at the neutrality temperature `Tn` and reports the
energy needed to do so:

```{python}
dataAC = wall.solveAC()
dataAC = pd.concat([dataAC, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)

print(f"cooling_energy = {wall.cooling_energy:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.cooling_energy/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
print(f"heating_energy = {wall.heating_energy:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.heating_energy/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
```

```{python}
plot_day(dataAC, title="Same wall, air-conditioned (Ti = Tn) — May, Cuernavaca")
```
